DATE:         DECEMBER 30, 1987

SUBJECT:      Section 12-10 Zoning Resolution
              Predominantly Built-Up Area and Block
              Cemeteries



The In-Fill zoning provisions may be applicable when a construction site
is located on block which meets the criteria contained in both the
definition of Block and the definition of Predominantly Built-Up Area
contained within Section 12-10 of the New York City Zoning Resolution.

      "A predominantly built-up area is a block having a maximum area of 4
      acres in R4 and R5 districts which is developed with buildings on
      zoning lots comprising 50 percent or more of the area of the block
      including a commercial district mapped within such residential
      district."

The above quoted portion of the definition shall be construed to require
that the entire block be limited to a maximum area of 4 acres and the
entire block also be zoned in R4 and R5 or both districts. Commercial
zones C1-1 through C1-5 and C2-1 through C2-5 may constitute part of the
block.

      "A block is a tract of land bounded by:

           (b) Public parks

           (d) Airport boundaries..."
The Zoning Maps are incorporated into the provisions of the Zoning
Resolution by Section 11-14. The maps show 'Public parks', airports
and cemeteries designated with the same symbol, a dash-dot. Each of
these uses may contain buildings but in general they involve similar
characteristics of open space.

For purposes of In-Fill Zoning and the determination of 'Block'
boundaries, cemeteries shall form such a boundary.
